about: The judge test set: questions with known answers, weighted toward the areas rulings commonly go wrong in. Each expected answer was checked against the CR effective with data/cr.json and the cards' current Oracle text and official rulings (scripts/judge-brief.ts), not from memory. mustSay: facts a correct answer has to state (in any wording). mustNotSay: the usual wrong answers. api: one of the few also run through the real judge (scripts/judge-eval.ts).

questions.ask: My Urza's Saga has 2 lore counters (chapters I and II have resolved). My opponent resolves Blood Moon. What happens to the Saga on my next turn?
questions.ruling: It stays. As a Mountain it loses its chapter abilities, so no lore counter is added in my precombat main phase and it isn't sacrificed; it keeps the two abilities chapters I and II gave it, and also taps for {R}.
mustSay: Urza's Saga loses its chapter abilities (it loses the abilities from its rules text)
It keeps the abilities it gained from chapters I and II, because those were granted by an effect (CR 305.7 / the Urza's Saga ruling)
No lore counter is put on it: the precombat main phase action only applies to Sagas with one or more chapter abilities (CR 714.3c)
It isn't sacrificed: the sacrifice rule only applies to a Saga with one or more chapter abilities (CR 714.4)
It can tap for {R}

questions.ask: Opalescence came down first, then my opponent cast Humility. What are Humility and Opalescence now? Would it be different if Humility had come down first?
questions.ruling: Humility (later timestamp) wins in layer 7b: Humility is a 1/1 enchantment creature with no abilities, and Opalescence isn't a creature (it doesn't animate itself). If Humility had come first, Opalescence's later 7b effect makes Humility a 4/4 with no abilities.
mustSay: Opalescence doesn't affect itself, so it isn't a creature
Humility is a creature (Opalescence, layer 4) and loses its abilities (layer 6)
Both set base power and toughness in layer 7b, so timestamp order decides
Opalescence first then Humility: Humility is 1/1
Humility first then Opalescence: Humility is 4/4
Effects that started applying keep applying in later layers even after the ability is removed (CR 613.6)
mustNotSay: Humility stops working because it lost its own ability

questions.ask: What does Blood Moon do to Dryad Arbor?
questions.ruling: Dryad Arbor is nonbasic, so it becomes a Mountain instead of a Forest. It's still a 1/1 green Dryad creature land, and it taps for {R} (it's still a creature, so summoning sickness applies to tapping it).
mustSay: Dryad Arbor is a nonbasic land, so Blood Moon affects it
It loses the Forest type and becomes a Mountain; it taps for {R}, not {G}
It's still a creature (setting a land subtype doesn't remove card types, CR 305.7) and still a Dryad
It's still green (its color indicator isn't changed)
mustNotSay: It's unaffected because it's a Forest

questions.ask: My 2/2 has two +1/+1 counters and I already cast Giant Growth on it this turn. My opponent responds to my attack with Turn to Frog on it. How big is it?
questions.ruling: 6/6: Turn to Frog sets base power and toughness to 1/1 (layer 7b), then the counters (+2/+2) and Giant Growth (+3/+3) still apply in layer 7c, whenever they started. It has no abilities and is a blue Frog until end of turn.
mustSay: Turn to Frog sets base P/T to 1/1 (layer 7b)
Counters and Giant Growth still apply on top (layer 7c), no matter when they started
It's a 6/6
It loses all abilities and is a blue Frog until end of turn
sources: Turn to Frog ruling 2014-07-18 (Titanic Growth, counters)

questions.ask: I control Hardened Scales and Doubling Season. An effect puts one +1/+1 counter on my creature. How many does it get?
questions.ruling: I choose the order (it's my creature). Hardened Scales first, then Doubling Season: (1+1)x2 = 4. The other order gives 3. So 4 if I want.
mustSay: The creature's controller (me) chooses the order to apply the replacement effects (CR 616.1)
Scales then Season gives 4 counters
Season then Scales gives 3 counters
sources: Hardened Scales ruling 2023-09-01 (you choose the order)

questions.ask: My opponent has Leyline of the Void. My Kitchen Finks gets destroyed. Does persist bring it back?
questions.ruling: No. Finks is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, so it never dies and persist doesn't trigger.
mustSay: Kitchen Finks is exiled instead of being put into the graveyard
It doesn't die, so persist doesn't trigger
sources: Leyline of the Void ruling 2024-09-20 (nontoken creatures won't die)

questions.ask: Rest in Peace is out and my commander gets destroyed. Can it go back to the command zone? Do my 'whenever a creature dies' triggers go off?
questions.ruling: It's exiled instead (it doesn't die, so dies triggers don't trigger), and then I may move it from exile to the command zone as a state-based action.
mustSay: The commander is exiled instead of going to the graveyard
It didn't die, so dies triggers don't trigger
I may put it into the command zone from exile (CR 903.9a, a state-based action)
mustNotSay: It goes to the command zone instead of being exiled, so it died

questions.ask: I'm at -3 life with Platinum Angel out. My opponent kills the Angel. What happens?
questions.ruling: While I controlled the Angel I couldn't lose. Once it's gone, the next time state-based actions are checked I'm still at 0 or less life, so I lose.
mustSay: While I control Platinum Angel I can't lose the game, even at 0 or less life
Once it leaves, I lose the next time state-based actions are checked if my life is still 0 or less (CR 704.5a)
mustNotSay: I lose immediately when the spell is cast

questions.ask: I have 3 cards left in my library. Thassa's Oracle enters; my only other blue is a permanent with {U}{U} in its mana cost. My opponent kills the Oracle in response to its trigger. Do I win?
questions.ruling: No. Devotion is counted as the ability resolves, and the Oracle only counts if it's still on the battlefield. Without it, devotion is 2, which is less than 3 cards, so I don't win (I look at the top 2 instead).
mustSay: Devotion is counted when the ability resolves
The Oracle counts only if it's still on the battlefield then
Devotion is 2 and the library has 3 cards, so I don't win
mustNotSay: Devotion was locked in when it triggered
sources: Thassa's Oracle ruling 2020-01-24 (counted as the ability resolves)

questions.ask: I'm at 41 life with Felidar Sovereign. In my upkeep the trigger goes on the stack and my opponent Bolts me in response. Do I still win?
questions.ruling: No. It's an intervening 'if': it checks again on resolution, and at 38 life it does nothing.
mustSay: It's an intervening-if clause, checked both when it triggers and when it resolves (CR 603.4)
At 38 life the ability does nothing

questions.ask: I have Blood Artist and three other creatures; my opponent has two creatures. Wrath of God resolves. How many times does Blood Artist trigger?
questions.ruling: Six: it sees all six creatures die at the same time, including itself (leaves-the-battlefield abilities look back in time).
mustSay: Blood Artist triggers for itself and for each creature that died at the same time
Six triggers
Leaves-the-battlefield triggers look back in time (CR 603.10a)
mustNotSay: It doesn't trigger because it died too

questions.ask: It's my upkeep. I have Phyrexian Arena; my opponent has Sulfuric Vortex. I'm at 3 life. In what order do these resolve, and do I survive?
questions.ruling: APNAP: my Arena trigger goes on the stack first, then my opponent's Vortex trigger on top, so Vortex resolves first (3 to 1), then Arena (draw, lose 1, to 0). I lose.
mustSay: The active player's triggers go on the stack first, then the non-active player's (APNAP, CR 603.3b)
Sulfuric Vortex resolves first
I end at 0 life and lose
mustNotSay: I choose the order of both triggers

questions.ask: On my turn, before combat, I Ephemerate my creature that has Pacifism on it and two +1/+1 counters. What comes back, and can it attack?
questions.ruling: It returns as a new object: Pacifism goes to the graveyard and the counters are gone. It can't attack this turn, because I haven't controlled it continuously since the start of my turn.
mustSay: It returns as a new object (CR 400.7)
Pacifism goes to the graveyard and the +1/+1 counters are gone
It can't attack this turn (summoning sickness, CR 302.6)

questions.ask: My opponent casts Doom Blade on my creature. I respond with Cloudshift on it. What happens to the Doom Blade?
questions.ruling: The returned creature is a new object, so Doom Blade's only target is illegal: Doom Blade doesn't resolve and does nothing.
mustSay: The creature that returns is a new object (CR 400.7)
Doom Blade's target is illegal, so it doesn't resolve (CR 608.2b)
mustNotSay: Doom Blade destroys the returned creature
Doom Blade is countered by Cloudshift

questions.ask: Can I target my own hexproof creature with Swords to Plowshares?
questions.ruling: Yes. Hexproof only stops spells and abilities your opponents control from targeting it.
mustSay: Yes
Hexproof only stops opponents' spells and abilities (CR 702.11)

questions.ask: I cast Electrolyze dealing 1 damage to each of two creatures. One of them leaves the battlefield before it resolves. What happens?
questions.ruling: It still resolves: the remaining creature is dealt 1 damage (not 2) and I draw a card.
mustSay: The damage division is set when it's cast
The remaining target is dealt 1 damage, not 2
I still draw a card
mustNotSay: It fizzles and I don't draw

questions.ask: I cast Vapor Snag on my opponent's creature; they respond with Blossoming Defense on it. Do they still lose 1 life?
questions.ruling: No. Its only target is now illegal, so Vapor Snag doesn't resolve and none of it happens, including the life loss.
mustSay: The creature gains hexproof, so it's an illegal target
Vapor Snag doesn't resolve and none of its effects happen, including the life loss (CR 608.2b)

questions.ask: I play a second Thalia, Guardian of Thraben. My first one is indestructible. Do I have to get rid of one, and does that count as dying?
questions.ruling: Yes: the legend rule makes me choose one; the other is put into the graveyard. That's not destruction, so indestructible doesn't help, and it does count as dying.
mustSay: I choose one to keep and the other goes to the graveyard (the legend rule, CR 704.5j)
It isn't destroyed, so indestructible doesn't save it
Being put into the graveyard from the battlefield is dying, so dies triggers trigger
mustNotSay: The indestructible one can't be removed

questions.ask: My Darksteel Myr gets -1/-1 until end of turn. It's indestructible, so it survives, right?
questions.ruling: No. With 0 toughness it's put into the graveyard as a state-based action; that isn't destruction, so indestructible doesn't stop it.
mustSay: It's put into the graveyard for having 0 toughness (CR 704.5f)
That isn't destruction, so indestructible doesn't help

questions.ask: We're both at 2 life. I cast Earthquake for 2. Who wins?
questions.ruling: Nobody: both players reach 0 at the same time and lose simultaneously, so the game is a draw.
mustSay: Both players lose at the same time
The game is a draw (CR 104.4a)
mustNotSay: I win because it's my spell

questions.ask: I Clone my opponent's 3/3 that has two +1/+1 counters and Rancor on it. What does my Clone look like?
questions.ruling: A plain 3/3 copy: copy effects take only the copiable values (the printed card), not counters or Aura effects. No trample, no counters.
mustSay: Clone copies only the copiable values (CR 707.2)
It's a 3/3 with no counters
It doesn't get Rancor's +2/+0 or trample

questions.ask: My opponent casts Fireball with X=5 at my face. I Twincast it. What's X for my copy, and can I point it at them?
questions.ruling: The copy has X=5 too, and I may choose new targets for it, so I can aim it at my opponent.
mustSay: The copy has the same X (5) (CR 707.10)
I may choose new targets, so yes

questions.ask: I've cast my commander from the command zone twice already. It got bounced to my hand. How much extra does it cost now, from my hand?
questions.ruling: Nothing extra: commander tax only applies when casting it from the command zone. (Cast from the command zone it would be {4} more.)
mustSay: Commander tax only applies to casting from the command zone (CR 903.8)
From the hand there's no tax
mustNotSay: It costs {4} more from my hand

questions.ask: My opponent's commander hit me for 12 combat damage, then died and went to the command zone. They recast it and it hit me for 9 more. Am I dead?
questions.ruling: Yes. Commander damage counts per commander over the whole game, through zone changes: 21 total, so I lose.
mustSay: Commander damage is tracked per commander over the course of the game (CR 903.10a)
Zone changes don't reset it
21 total, so I lose
mustNotSay: It reset when it went to the command zone

questions.ask: Player B stole player A's commander with Control Magic and hit me with it. Does that combat damage count toward commander damage, and whose?
questions.ruling: Yes: it's still the same commander, whoever controls it. It counts toward the 21 from that commander.
mustSay: It counts: commander damage is by the commander, whoever controls it
It adds to the total from that one commander
mustNotSay: It doesn't count because B doesn't own it

questions.ask: Can I play Figure of Destiny in my mono-red Commander deck? I'd only ever pay red for it.
questions.ruling: No. Its mana symbols include {R/W} hybrid, so its color identity is red and white, which doesn't fit a mono-red commander.
mustSay: Color identity counts every mana symbol in its mana cost and rules text, including hybrid (CR 903.4)
Its color identity is red and white
Not allowed in mono-red
mustNotSay: Yes, because hybrid can be paid with red
sources: Figure of Destiny color identity RW

questions.ask: My opponent has Thalia, Guardian of Thraben; I have Baral, Chief of Compliance. What does Lightning Bolt cost me?
questions.ruling: {R}: start from {R}, Thalia adds {1}, then Baral takes off {1}.
mustSay: Increases are added, then reductions applied (CR 601.2f)
It costs {R}

questions.ask: With Omniscience out, can I cast Stroke of Genius for free with X=10?
questions.ruling: I can cast it for free, but X must be 0 when casting without paying the mana cost.
mustSay: Casting without paying the mana cost means X is 0 (CR 107.3b)
mustNotSay: I pay X and Omniscience covers the rest

questions.ask: My opponent has Thalia. Can I still Force of Will for its alternative cost, and what do I pay?
questions.ruling: Yes, but Thalia's tax applies to the alternative cost: 1 life, exile a blue card, and {1}.
mustSay: Cost increases apply to alternative costs too (CR 601.2f)
I pay 1 life, exile a blue card and {1}
mustNotSay: Thalia doesn't affect the alternative cost

questions.ask: My opponent taps Birds of Paradise for mana to cast something. Can I Bolt the Birds in response so they don't get the mana?
questions.ruling: No. Mana abilities don't use the stack and can't be responded to; the mana is already made. To stop it I'd have to kill the Birds earlier, when I have priority.
mustSay: Mana abilities don't use the stack (CR 605.3)
You can't respond to it; they get the mana

questions.ask: My 5/5 with deathtouch and trample is blocked by a 4/4. How much can I trample over?
questions.ruling: 4: with deathtouch, 1 damage counts as lethal to the blocker, so I assign 1 to it and 4 to the player.
mustSay: With deathtouch, any nonzero damage counts as lethal for assigning trample damage (CR 702.2c)
1 to the blocker, 4 to the player

questions.ask: My 3/3 attacker (no trample) got blocked, then my opponent sacrificed the blocker. Does my creature deal damage to them?
questions.ruling: No. It stays blocked even with no blocker left, so without trample it deals no combat damage.
mustSay: It remains a blocked creature (CR 509.1h)
Without trample it deals no combat damage

questions.ask: My 4/4 with double strike and trample is blocked by a 2/2. How much damage does the defending player take?
questions.ruling: 6: first-strike damage is 2 to the blocker and 2 to the player; the blocker dies, and in the regular damage step all 4 go to the player, since a blocked trampler with no blockers assigns all its damage to the player.
mustSay: First strike damage step: 2 to the blocker, 2 to the player
Regular damage step: all 4 to the player (CR 702.19d)
6 total
mustNotSay: It deals no damage in the second step

questions.ask: My opponent casts Krosan Grip on my artifact. Can I sacrifice it to its own ability in response? Can I tap it for mana?
questions.ruling: I can't activate its non-mana abilities while a split second spell is on the stack, but I can activate mana abilities (and special actions like turning a face-down creature up).
mustSay: Split second stops casting spells and activating non-mana abilities (CR 702.61a)
So no sacrificing it with a non-mana ability (a sacrifice ability that is itself a mana ability, like Lotus Petal's, still works: CR 702.61b, 605.1a)
Mana abilities are still allowed
mustNotSay: I can sacrifice it in response

questions.ask: It's night. I cast two spells during my turn. What happens with day and night?
questions.ruling: As the next turn begins (in the untap step), it becomes day, because the previous turn's active player cast two or more spells.
mustSay: It becomes day as the next turn begins (untap step, CR 502.2)
Because the active player cast two or more spells that turn

questions.ask: Four-player game. Player C is the monarch and concedes during player B's turn. Who's the monarch now?
questions.ruling: Player B, the active player, becomes the monarch as C leaves the game.
mustSay: The active player becomes the monarch (CR 725.4)
So B

questions.ask: My opponent has the initiative. My creature deals combat damage to them. What happens?
questions.ruling: I take the initiative, and taking it triggers a venture into Undercity (an inherent triggered ability, so it uses the stack), without waiting for my upkeep.
mustSay: I take the initiative (CR 726.2)
Taking it makes me venture into Undercity (it triggers on taking the initiative, not only at upkeep)
mustNotSay: I venture only at my next upkeep

questions.ask: Is Mana Crypt legal in Commander?
questions.ruling: No, it's banned in Commander.
mustSay: Banned in Commander

questions.ask: Competitive REL. My opponent forgot their own trigger that would have helped them, and I noticed. Do I have to tell them? Is it a penalty?
questions.ruling: No, I don't have to point out my opponent's triggers. It's Game Play Error - Missed Trigger for the opponent; no penalty for a trigger that would have benefited them.
mustSay: I'm not required to point out my opponent's missed triggers
The infraction is Game Play Error - Missed Trigger (IPG 2.1)
Cites the IPG
mustNotSay: I get a penalty for not pointing it out

questions.ask: How does Glimmerwing Sovereign interact with Blood Moon?
questions.ruling: There's no such card: it should say it couldn't find Glimmerwing Sovereign, not invent its text.
mustSay: It couldn't find the card
mustNotSay: Any rules text for Glimmerwing Sovereign stated as fact
